parsed.why: Same-sex conduct carries a five-year minimum, though current enforcement is reportedly limited. Severe documented stigma and past police harassment add risk, but the record lacks trans-specific targeting evidence.

No trans-specific criminalisation, police-targeting pattern, or facility restriction is documented. Weak resident protections and poor attitudes toward same-sex marriage are climate signals; one local third-gender tradition is positive but not nationally representative.

Nationwide criminalisation, northern death-penalty provisions, police extortion and mass raids create state-backed targeting. Dating-app entrapment and an unprosecuted trans woman's killing add severe, current exposure.

No criminalisation is documented, but reports describe hostility, service denial and commonplace lynchings, with police rarely pursuing attackers. The violence evidence is unquantified and mostly not trans-specific, but recourse appears weak.

A court nationwide decriminalised same-sex conduct and interpreted constitutional sex equality to include gender identity. No trans-specific targeting or visitor-facing restrictions are documented; absent gender recognition and explicit protections are mainly resident-facing gaps.
